newsitem.title: UK: Iraq Feb Kirkuk exports scheduled slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Iraq Feb Kirkuk exports scheduled slightly lower.

text.p: The loading programme for Iraqi Kirkuk crude in February contains few surprises for the European sour crude market, with total liftings and likely spot availabilities just slightly down from January, oil traders said on Tuesday.

Iraq's State oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) has scheduled 11 cargoes carrying 9.4 million barrels, or 335,000 barrels per day (bpd), from Turkey's Mediterranean pipeline outlet at Ceyhan in February, down 25,000 bpd from the 13 cargoes of just over 11 million barrels total in January.
"It's not a significant change," said one contract holder.
Some 160,000 bpd of February liftings are under contract to major European oil companies and destined for their own refineries in northwest Europe and the Mediterranean.
Nearly 70,000 bpd of the volume is set to remain in Turkey, under contract to state refiner Tupras.
Russian oil companies and traders will lift the remaining 105,000 bpd, of which around half is expected to be offered on the European spot market.
"I'd say about 50 percent is already committed to either Europe or the U.S.," said one Kirkuk lifter. "But there should be bits and pieces (offered on a spot basis)."
In January, a VLCC of Kirkuk crude, made up of two separate parcels contracted to Russian lifters was widely heard to have been resold by a Swiss-based trader to a major Rotterdam refiner.
This sale, together with the rumoured trade of another smaller cargo into Rotterdam, translated into 60,000 to 90,000 bpd of spot sales in January.
There were no disruptions to Ceyhan loadings in January, traders said.
"There weren't any problems and I don't foresee any," said one trader. "There is plenty of capacity (at Ceyhan) and this is peanuts compared to what they dealt with (before the Gulf War)."
Under the United Nations oil-for-food agreement, Iraq began exporting crude from Ceyhan and the Gulf port of Mina al-Bakr in December.
Al-Bakr sales of Basrah Light were thought to total around 200,000 bpd for January.
